svg.text: A2 CEILING-QUILL FMC — a food machining centre
One spindle hangs from a flat sealed ceiling of two eccentric discs; all tools are passive and wait in self-washing holsters.
wet cell 540 W × 520 D × 750 H (module 600 W)
8 axes per quill (15 for two quills)
quill Ø 50, Z 380 mm, 3 kN · spindle 20 Nm / 9000 rpm
D1 disc Ø 500 (slewing ring, worm drive)
D1 turns, D2 turns inside it → the quill (dot) reaches any
point of the deck; only two round seals face the food
ram pushes, grid cuts strips, the turning vessel rim cuts cubes
All tools are passive parts: the spindle nose brings torque, a push rod and water/air
each tool is rinsed in its own holster pocket (drain, 3 jets, warm air) within 2 min of use
1/8 The quill moves over the holster row and clicks onto the tongs: the two ceiling discs turn, the quill only goes up and down.
2/8 Tongs take the potato standing in the orienting cone and drop it into the dice cassette.
3/8 Tool change: tongs back into their holster, the ram foot picked up.
4/8 The ram pushes the potato through the 10 mm grid; the blade on the turning vessel rim cuts cubes into the vessel.
5/8 The ram goes back to its holster and is rinsed there by three jets; the turner is picked up.
6/8 The turner slides under the steak in the pan, lifts it 40 mm and the spindle turns it over.
7/8 Vessels and dies leave for the wash chamber; the quill picks the rotary jet head.
8/8 The cell washes itself by program: the jet head runs a fixed path 100 mm from every surface (≈ 18 min, 16 L).
